text:
Troy Terry missed the first month of Anaheim's season recovering from hip surgery and made his debut on Nov. 11, joining a Ducks team that TSN described as "red-hot" at the time. Three games in, he has one assist, three shots and about 13 minutes a night, roughly five fewer than he played last season. That is a player being eased back in, and nothing in those numbers says much about where he is headed.

What he was before the surgery is the better guide. Terry had 57 points in 61 games last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among forwards at driving play once teammates, opponents and zone starts are accounted for. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows how he does it: he carries the puck into the offensive zone on 60% of his entries, and carry-ins lead to a scoring chance far more often than dump-ins. He was also in the 85th percentile for setting up teammates' shots.

Our talent range for his scoring rate sits well above his current pace. We'd watch the ice time: as his minutes climb, we'll learn how much of the old Terry is back.
headline: Troy Terry is back, and three games is nothing
